findings.text: A weak page content comparator is provided that briefly maps two pages locally, compares one full page span, releases the mappings in reverse order, and reports the ordering outcome. It underlies ordering decisions in both stable and unstable searches.

Search of the node-local unstable ordering for content equal to a candidate page, descending by comparison outcome with scheduling latitude, rejecting self matches arising from forking, gating cross-node reuse on a global setting, and on miss marking and sequencing the supplied tracker and linking it as a new ordered entry while accounting an unshared page.

Stable and unstable orderings are partitioned per memory node with the partition chosen from the frame number under consideration, and scan restart clears every unstable partition while stable partitions persist. Node identity is recorded on new entries where NUMA awareness is enabled.

Stable content collisions use promotion of a solitary entry into a chain container holding duplicate entries, with later duplicates appended to that chain. A collapsed chain is observationally identical to no chain, stale entries met during descent force a fresh descent from the root, and displaced or misplaced duplicates are parked on a dedicated migration queue.

Trackers carry address-derived state where unstable membership and stable membership use distinct markers plus a scan sequence component for unstable entries, with node identity where applicable and ordered-list linkage by masked address. Promotion to stable moves the tracker onto a hash list owned by the stable entry and records that entry as owner.

Global accounting distinguishes unshared insertions, first sharer versus additional sharers on a stable entry, per-space merging totals, plus progress totals for examined and skipped pages. The choice between shared and sharing increments depends on whether the stable list already held a member.

Merging proceeds from placement validation and early exit for already-stable associations, through a stability gate based on repeated checksum equality and a zero-page fast path, then stable lookup followed by unstable lookup. Stable success attaches to the found entry, unstable success merges the pair and creates one stable entry owning both trackers, while same-folio collision triggers a deferred split attempt and stable-insert failure dissolves sharing on both sides.

Stable lookup may report busy without side effects, restart when concurrent rebalance invalidated position, return without insertion when no migratory candidate exists, replace or append via the migration queue when placement changed, and otherwise link the migratory candidate into the ordering. Reference acquisition on return depends on sharing candidacy, and evicted duplicates are requeued for migration.

Appending a tracker to a stable entry requires a non-negative sharing count, increments that count, warns once on exceeding a configurable sharing maximum unless bypassed for fork-like cases, and updates both global sharing tallies and per-space merging totals.

Stable insertion and attachment hold folio protection across tree mutation, with a non-blocking attempt preferred for the same-folio split path to avoid stalling when contended. Table descent releases its spin protection on every exit including absent mappings, space read protection spans the walk and is dropped before global list mutation, global list mutation uses spin protection, and background scanning holds a dedicated thread mutex.

The walk result carrier aggregates a referenced folio with its constituent page and the virtual address where found. The walk operation table selects a middle-level handler and requests read-locked traversal.

Full scanning cycles through registered spaces in list order, refreshing unstable state and pruning migrated stable entries at wrap plus draining per-cpu caches, then within each space visiting only mergeable regions and locating the next present anonymous non-device page at or after the cursor. Obsolete trackers beyond the cursor are discarded, spaces with no mergeable regions are detached and dereferenced, and sequence numbering advances once per complete cycle with start and stop notifications.

The background thread runs freezable at reduced priority, waits while an offline indicator is set, performs a bounded burst of merges when merging is enabled and work exists, then sleeps with timeout sensitive to interval changes when runnable or waits indefinitely for runnable or stop otherwise.

Smart scanning never skips when disabled, nor for pages already marked deduplicated nor trackers already flagged stable. Otherwise an age counter advances toward saturation, young ages are always processed, and older ages receive a stepped skip budget that grows with age to a fixed ceiling, with each skipped visit removing the tracker from its tree and counting the skip.

Hazards include rebalancing underfoot requiring restart, busy acquisition requiring abort without mutation, self comparison after forking requiring rejection, cross-node reuse requiring explicit enablement, allocation failure requiring null return with caller-side sharing dissolution, same large folio merging requiring reference-correct split retry, lockless middle-table reads requiring revalidation under protection, and list-empty races with concurrent exit requiring recheck after locking.

Symbolic control names observed include unstable and stable membership markers, a sequence mask, merge-enable and offline run flags, folio acquisition modes for locked versus try-lock versus no-lock access, mergeable area marking, huge-page leaf handling, and read-locked walk mode. Exact numeric encodings are not shown in these fragments.

Bounded scan driver that processes up to a caller-supplied page budget while the thread is not freezing, fetching the next tracker with its page, attempting merge, releasing the reference, and counting each examined page, stopping early when no further tracker exists.

Tracker allocation for a scan address reuses an existing entry on masked-address match, discards and frees lower-addressed predecessors after detaching them from trees, otherwise allocates a fresh zeroed entry associated with the current space, linked in address order with usage accounting.
Offline waiting has two build-dependent forms, one that releases the thread mutex and sleeps on the offline indicator until cleared before reacquiring, and one that performs no waiting.

Middle-level and leaf descent accept only present mappings whose normalized page belongs to an anonymous non-device folio, adjust sub-page position within large mappings by offset, acquire a reference before releasing spin protection, and distinguish absence from errors with a one-time warning on unexpected negative descent status.
